newsitem.title: USA: Israel, Palestinians each blamed for crisis - poll.
newsitem.headline: Israel, Palestinians each blamed for crisis - poll.

text.p: Americans are blaming Israel and the Palestinians about equally for the current Middle East turmoil over Israel's moves to build housing in East Jerusalem, according to a poll released on Wednesday.

Asked in a current Harris Poll who is more to blame for the current problems, 28 percent blamed the Israeli government of Benjamin Netanyahu while 31 percent blamed Palestinian authorities. Others either did not know or said both sides were equally to blame.
Similarly, 35 percent said Netanyahu was keeping agreements with Palestinians while 48 percent said he was breaking them and the remainder did not know or did not answer.
Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat was breaking agreements in the opinion of about 50 percent of those polled while 33 percent said he was keeping them.
In a commentary on the survey, pollster Humphrey Taylor said "Netanyahu may have done more to undermine American support for Israel than any Israeli leader since the birth of the country in 1948."
He said that most of the time since then Americans have been overwhelmingly supportive of Israel and very critical of Palestinians.
"Now for the first time, the public is more of less equally critical of both the Israeli government and the Palestinian authorities," Taylor wrote.
The poll was taken among 639 adults between March 26 and April 1 who had heard of the current crisis. The poll had a margin of error among this group of plus or minus four percentage points.
